info.title: Foundry API v1
info.description:
The JSON API of a Foundry instance, under /api/v1. Every operation except reading this description needs a machine token (the `machineToken` scheme). Every JSON error answer is the `Error` envelope.

An address under /api/v1 that is not one of the operations listed here answers 404 with the uniform not-found envelope, `{"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"not found"}}`, and checks no credential.

The order in which refusals are given:

1. An address under /api/v1 that is not an operation answers 404, with no authentication.
2. On an operation's path, a method the path does not offer answers 405 with an empty body and an `Allow` header, with no authentication. The exception is this description's own path, which answers the 404 envelope.
3. On an operation's path, a missing or bad token answers 401 before any 400, 413, 415 or 422.
4. When revoking a token, 429 can come before 403. No order is promised between them.

get.description: Answers this document, the same bytes for every caller of one release: the copy committed in the repository at crates/foundry-api/openapi.json. It needs no credential and checks none, so a missing, bad or revoked token gets the same answer. HEAD answers the same headers with no body. Any other method answers the uniform 404 envelope.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-cache`: a client revalidates, so it sees a new release's description.

post.description: Creates an issue in the project and answers it. The title is trimmed; an empty title and one over 256 characters both answer 422 `title_required`. The description is optional, defaults to empty, and over 262,144 characters answers 422 `description_too_long`. A refused request creates nothing.

422.description: Unprocessable. Two kinds of answer share this status. A JSON body that lacks a required field or has a field of the wrong type is refused by the server framework with plain text, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract. A title that is empty or over 256 characters, or a description over 262,144 characters, answers the `Error` envelope, with one of the codes below.

patch.summary: Move an issue to another lane
patch.description: Moves the issue to one of its project's lanes and answers the issue. `state` names the lane by its slug; each project has its own lanes, so there is no fixed list. `in-progress` and `canceled` are accepted for `in_progress` and `cancelled`. A lane the project does not have answers 422 `invalid_state`. A refused request changes nothing.

parameters.name: team_slug
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: project_slug
parameters.description: The project's slug, within the team.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The issue's number within its project. Anything but an integer answers 400.

requestBody.description: The lane to move the issue to.

200.description: The issue, in its new lane.

get.description: Answers every machine token of the workspace, newest first, revoked and expired ones included. The list is the whole workspace's; the team and project in the address must exist and be reachable by your token, but do not narrow it. An entry never carries a token's value. Only a workspace admin's token may list tokens. This API has no way to create a token: a workspace admin mints one, signed in to Foundry, at /admin/tokens.

parameters.name: team_slug
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: project_slug
parameters.description: The project's slug, within the team.

200.description: The workspace's machine tokens, newest first. No tokens answers an empty array.

403.description: Forbidden. The token's person is not a workspace admin. This is decided before the team and project are looked up.

delete.description: Revokes one machine token of the workspace. From then on that token is refused with 401; no other token changes. Revoking a token that is already revoked answers 204 again and changes nothing: the token keeps its first revocation time. Only a workspace admin's token may revoke, and a person may revoke only so many tokens in a short time; past that, the answer is 429 until the limit allows more, and it can come before 403.

parameters.name: team_slug
parameters.description: The team's slug.

parameters.name: project_slug
parameters.description: The project's slug, within the team.

parameters.name: jti
parameters.description: The token's id, its `jti`, as listed. Anything but a UUID answers 400.

204.description: Revoked, or already revoked. The answer has no body.

403.description: Forbidden. The token's person is not a workspace admin. This is decided before the team and project are looked up.

429.description: Too many requests. The token's person has revoked too many tokens in a short time; try again later. Nothing was revoked.

error.message: too many token revocations; slow down

machineToken.description: A machine token: an EdDSA-signed JWT sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A workspace admin mints one, signed in to Foundry, at /admin/tokens; the value is shown once. This API lists and revokes tokens but cannot create one.

Error.description: Every JSON error answer has this shape. `code` is stable and machine-readable; `message` is for people.

ErrorDetail.description: The detail of an error answer.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable code, such as `not_found` or `title_required`.

message.description: A short text for people. It may change between releases.

key.description: The issue's key: the project's key prefix, a hyphen and the number.

number.description: The issue's number within its project.

examples: Sign-in times out behind the proxy

state.description: The lane the issue is in, by its slug. Each project has its own lanes; the defaults are backlog, todo, in_progress, done and cancelled. `in-progress` and `canceled` are accepted as aliases.

CreateIssueRequest.description: The body of a request to create an issue.

title.description: The issue's title: 1 to 256 characters after trimming.
examples: Sign-in times out behind the proxy

description.description: The issue's description, in Markdown, up to 262,144 characters. Optional; it defaults to empty.
examples: Seen from the CI runners only.

PatchIssueRequest.description: The body of a request to move an issue to another lane.

state.description: The slug of one of the issue's project's lanes. `in-progress` and `canceled` are accepted as aliases.

CommentBodyRequest.description: The body of a request to add or edit a comment.

body.description: The comment, in Markdown: not empty after trimming, and up to 65,536 characters.
examples: Seen again on the staging proxy.

author_email.description: The email of the comment's author.

body_html.description: The comment rendered from its Markdown and sanitised.

edited.description: Whether the comment was edited after it was written.

IssueHistoryEntry.description: One recorded change of an issue.

actor.description: The email of the person whose call made the change.

old.description: The value before the change, or null where there was none.

at.description: When the change was made, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

Token.description: One machine token of the workspace, as listed. It never carries the token's value.

jti.description: The token's id, a UUID. Revoke the token by it.

label.description: The name the admin gave the token when minting it.

scope_team_id.description: The id of the one team the token reaches, or null when it reaches the whole workspace.

scope_team_name.description: The name of that team, or null when the token reaches the whole workspace or the team no longer exists.

expires_at.description: When the token stops working, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

revoked.description: Whether the token has been revoked.

last_used_at.description: When the token was last used, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, or null if it never was.

minted_by.description: The email of the admin who minted the token, or null when that is no longer known.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized. The machine token is missing, malformed, expired, revoked, unknown or not signed by this instance's key; the answer does not say which. Also answered when the token cannot be checked.

NotFound.description: Not found. The same answer, byte for byte, for a team, project, issue or comment that does not exist, one your token cannot reach, and a path that is not part of the API.

MethodNotAllowed.description: Method not allowed. The path exists but does not offer this method. The body is empty, and no credential is checked.

Allow.description: The methods the path offers, such as `GET,HEAD`.

Internal.description: Internal error. Something failed inside the server; the answer carries no detail.

BadPath.description: Bad request. A path segment does not parse: an issue number that is not an integer, or a comment or token id that is not a UUID. The body is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.

BadBody.description: Bad request. The body is not valid JSON. The body of this answer is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Payload too large. The body is larger than 2 MB, and is refused before it is read. The answer is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: Unsupported media type. The request does not carry `Content-Type: application/json`. The answer is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.

UnprocessableBody.description: Unprocessable body. The JSON body lacks a required field or has a field of the wrong type. The answer is plain text from the server framework, not the `Error` envelope, and its wording is not part of the contract.
